subject: AuroraBank SIG intake: SDLC release-notary + keystore artifacts
messages:
From: Maya Singh <m.singh@aurorabank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: AuroraBank Security <security@aurorabank.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG intake: SDLC release-notary + keystore/CI artifacts request

Ben —

Thanks for taking this on. As part of AuroraBank's SIG intake we need a short, tangible evidence bundle showing how Redwood handles secure releases (code review gating, CI/CD controls, secrets/keystore stewardship, and change approvals). Auditor asks for the following items or pointers to them: 

- Short sampling of PRs (merged in last 90 days) with reviewer/approval history and any gating comments (redact sensitive code).
- CI runbook snapshot showing job user/service-account separation, privileged steps, and rollback controls.
- Keystore rotation logs for the past quarter (timestamps + operator id).
- Change approval chronology for a recent release (who requested, approver, timestamp).
- High-level mapping that ties each artifact back to SIG/SOC2 control IDs (just 1-2 lines per artifact).

Can you confirm these items and provide them by end of day Friday (2026-07-17)? Our assessor is Laura Chen (laura.chen@assesscorp.com). If you need to redact anything, please note what was removed.

Maya
Security Intake — AuroraBank

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@aurorabank.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG intake: SDLC release-notary + keystore/CI artifacts request

Maya —

Appreciate the clear list. We'll get a focused bundle over to Laura by EOD Friday. Quick notes on scope and approach: 

- We'll provide a small PR sample (3 PRs) with reviewer timestamps and merge approvals; sensitive code will be redacted and replaced with placeholders, and we'll include a redaction log.
- Attaching a CI runbook snapshot (ci-runbook-snapshot-20260714.zip) that highlights job separation and promoted-artifacts flow.
- Keystore rotation log (keystore-rotation-log-2026Q2.pdf) is included; we've redacted remote IPs and operator MFA tokens.
- Change approval chronology is exported as change-approval-chronology-202606.csv (one recent release).
- We'll include a short mapping doc inline in the email body and link to the Drive folder for full manifests.

Action items for us: Irene will assemble cryptographic custody notes and map to SIG control IDs; Jordan will export the PR sample and the CI snapshots. I'll attach the initial artifacts now. If Laura needs signed attestations we can include a brief DocuSign for the keystore handback.

Ben
Senior Solutions — Redwood Inference
(attachment: ci-runbook-snapshot-20260714.zip)
(attachment: code-review-sample-PRs-redacted.csv)

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Maya Singh <m.singh@aurorabank.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SIG intake: SDLC release-notary + keystore/CI artifacts request

Hi Maya — forwarding the artifacts Ben attached and adding the control mapping and custody notes below. See also the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sdlc-evidence).

-- control mapping (high level) --
PR sample (code-review-sample-PRs-redacted.csv) => maps to SIG-PR-01 / SOC2 CC6.1 (peer review, approval policy). Notes: we removed full diffs, replaced with redaction placeholders; redaction log included as first column of CSV.

CI runbook (ci-runbook-snapshot-20260714.zip) => maps to SIG-CI-03 / SOC2 CC6.2 (separation of duties, least privilege for runner accounts, promoted artifact signing). The snapshot contains pipeline YAML excerpts that show guarded deploy steps and the rollback job. Jenkins ephemeral-runner accounts are time-limited; we include an excerpt quoting the TTL enforcement.

Keystore rotation (keystore-rotation-log-2026Q2.pdf) => maps to SIG-KMS-02 / SOC2 CC7.3 (key rotation history + operator IDs). We scrubbed session tokens and IPs; operator IDs are internal UIDs. If the assessor needs unsuppressed operator identifiers we can provide them via an encrypted transfer and after an NDA addendum.

Change approvals (change-approval-chronology-202606.csv) => maps to SIG-CHG-01 / SOC2 CC5.4 (change control, approval chain). The CSV includes requestor, approver, timestamp, and brief justification. We removed runbook links that contain secrets.

Additional notes on secrets management:
- All long-lived secrets are in our KMS-backed vault (kms-managed-keys).
- CI jobs use short-lived tokens issued by our ephemeral token service; logs proving TTL were pulled into the runbook snapshot.
- For cross-reference: JIRA ticket SUP-1234 contains the release playbook and is linked here: https://jira.example/browse/SUP-1234.

If Laura would like a 30-minute walkthrough of the artifacts, I'm available Thu 07/16 or Fri 07/17 09:00-12:00 PDT. Otherwise we'll upload a signed attestation and the redaction log to the Drive folder and mark them for reviewer access.

—Irene
Head of Security Assurance — Redwood Inference
(attachment: keystore-rotation-log-2026Q2.pdf)
(attachment: change-approval-chronology-202606.csv)

From: Maya Singh <m.singh@aurorabank.com>

Received, this looks good and the mapping is exactly what the assessor needs. A masked tie-out (approver display name + CI job id) is acceptable.

If you can drop that in the Drive folder by Friday morning we'll mark the intake as complete. Appreciate the quick turnaround. I'll loop Laura in the Drive permission once uploaded.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
